correctness.rationale: For each exterior point transform p=Lw, and parametrize the entire contact (n-2)-sphere by u=R^-2 w+sqrt(1-R^-2)z with z unit orthogonal to w. The exact squared-length formula has an odd linear term; equality under z and -z forces Dw parallel to w. Equality of the remaining quadratic form on the full unit sphere of w-perp forces scalar compression. The result D=lambda P+mu(I-P) is both necessary and sufficient, and the explicit axial tangent length identity and inverse intercept follow by algebra. Dimensions n>=3, strict exterior, positive-definite axes, and converse are all handled. Eleven Python numerical scenarios verify normalization and sample spreads but are not relied on as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The equitangent observer locus is a natural classical invariant explicitly motivating the 2012 equal-tangents literature. The classification answers its entire fixed-ellipsoid realization problem in every n>=3, identifies the exact spectral symmetry boundary between empty, two-ray, and full-exterior loci, and provides a natural direct inverse reconstruction from the axial tangent-length profile. It includes nonexistence for triaxial ellipsoids, not merely a routine single example or parameter substitution. The distinction from the known planar behavior is geometrically meaningful.
